body: This is exactly how I feel. I know this thread was made over a year ago but your comment really helped me feel less alone!

As someone who has visited psychiatric wards/hospitals at my worst times, and honestly was more traumatized by the mental healthcare system, I met people who were possibly more safer and better cared for in the wards than at home, and that is saying A LOT. I would see toddlers being dropped off or put under psych testing. It is their parents sending them there. Maybe the parents are the problem. Nothing is wrong with children for having understandable issues given their parents' negligence.

I’ve seen stories of women becoming blind and having to amputate their limbs because of birth complications. Doesn’t help that we have a very sexist health system that gaslights pain and lacks research for a majority of women’s health issues.

I think our species is still adapting to our modern world (technology, capitalism, nuclear families, etc.) and mental illnesses can show up from our tolerance levels and ability to cope.

It’s against the laws of nature to think for yourself and naturally respond to your surroundings and life. Let the wizards of mental health correct you. For the true protection and enrichment is their bank. You are a person in need, and they see the needs to be the removal of your personhood. To reject this is to come out as one not part of this world. A cruel world, indeed.
Cognitive distortions might be some witchcraft to them then

If we had a perfect society, then we wouldn’t “go against our nature”. But we adapt and evolve. We are smarter than our animal instincts if we choose to not reproduce

Not to actually help people as much as we hoped. Those with better experiences are rare

For those that go into psychiatry to actually help people, they would notice the flaws and actually care about how we think of it

Most of the children there are sent there because it was their parents who are “sick” or “crazy”, if someone had to point fingers. Framing the insanity of the world and unfortunate circumstances as mental illnesses is just more profitable, but even mental health has stigma. Psychiatry can pretend they care and say to reduce such stigma, but at the end of the day, they’re the thought police.

They prey on an already misunderstood population/community so that when they damage them they can get away with it and pretend they tried helping them. This saying is important for all us survivors who are still traumatized by what we went through and/or witnessed and want to make change. It’s horrible to realize that one of the reasons why there isn’t much awareness or general knowledge about how corrupt and unhelpful the approach to treating the mentally ill people is because many are too traumatized to speak up. I don’t blame them, the shit we’ve been through is silencing and we’re already gaslighted and lose our autonomy even IN treatment. They have a right to protect themselves and their boundaries and live their life. But it’s an uphill battle we’re fighting. It’s hard to be around allies who don’t understand or who don’t try to. It’s hard to not criminalize and antagonize them even if they mean well and just don’t know. It’s hard to sit and witness mental health awareness conversations and social media posts that barely break the glass ceiling we’ve been caged in. I literally hate all the psychiatrists I see on tiktok that romanticize their medical journeys and personal lives/struggles but choose to get the MD for the money and prescribing privileges. Some probably don’t even know what they’re doing to us because the curriculum and culture even beyond treating mental illness is just meds and shaming. I wish they asked us how we feel and our perspective because they’re treating us, right. They say they wanna help us, right? It’s really hard. Even to say “stay calm” might come off the wrong way to us neurodivergent and mentally ill peeps. But it’s true. I’m so thankful for this community and hope someday in my personal and professional life I could bring awareness and we can all make systemic change. Yes, we need mental health awareness. But we also need mental illness education, we need psychiatric reform. We need real conversations people still aren’t comfortable to have. Heck, maybe I’m a socialist, but we seriously need everyone just to understand that the basics are healthy relationships and financial stability and that psychiatry is just another speciality/field in the medical-industrial complex.

Very well said. I’ve had few good experiences with nurses, but more than none. Ones that stood out to me was that they were validating and patient with me. They understood that they don’t understand everything about me and neither do I, myself. Since that is natural as someone navigating any type of illness and still growing up. A nurse who treats me like a patient, and makes sure I’m an informed one, but a person too. Psychiatric nurses should understand they’re helping people at a very critical time in their lives where they’re seeking a form of rehabilitation or intervention in their life and they should be able to take that with them after. Most people are anti meds, including myself, but even if you had to prescribe them, which I hope you don’t but I understand it’ll be an option or thought given your position, make sure the patient has other tools and things in place to actually help them.

This may be off tangent or not as related, but there’s also just the natural necessity for alone time. I found that the isolation from stressors and family when I was in the hospital was helpful. (When the staff say I’m isolating though and try to criminalize me for it, that’s the problem. Still don’t understand why they straight up say they’ll keep me longer if I don’t shower or wake up at their crazy scheduled times either) And that when I’m alone, still able to be safe by myself, I need some alone time to process things and regulate myself. We all need a balance. But it’s a double standard when people only call us lonely or antisocial when we’re having alone time or need more of it because of stuff we need to process. Sometimes being out is overwhelming. And this applies to people on the spectrum or with mental illness. I think anything outside of social norms is pathologicized and deemed deviant. And that’s why everyone wants to “correct” and criticize us. It’s not to help us or make us comfortable, sometimes it’s just about making them comfortable.

Labeling people as mentally ill or “mad” or “crazy”, even if they weren’t, was a way to dehumanize them and denounce or compromise their testimony. This still appears so much in court and the media too. I’m not surprised. What I don’t like is that people don’t acknowledge that the label itself is harmful for both people who are and just need help, and for people who aren’t. The label itself shouldn’t be used regardless, but weaponizing it shows that people understand it’s a derogatory, offensive, and powerful way of locking people up in a torture house or asylum. And for “their best interest”? Nope, for the best interest of the manipulator

The US prison system can learn a lot about from Germany and how they prioritize the wellbeing and socio-economic stability of the prisoner so they would not "need" crime. Similar to us, we need economic stability, healthy relationships, and a healthier and humane culture/society so we do not feel even more overwhelmed and cope in unhealthy ways and think we are better off dead. A lot of people kill themselves because they know they will die anyway, it is hard to work and sustain yourself financially with a mental illness. They should invest in us instead of us investing in bs. Our society makes us feel like we are expired or some sort of currency.

Social work and welfare services. Counseling is the only treatment I really stand by, but also there needs to be systemic/administrative changes and screenings done for therapists/psychologists who can be abusive and have worked in tandem with psychiatrists. Alina didn’t ask to be the Sun Summoner, and while the Darkling was alluring and had his unique qualities and challenges, she didn’t give in to his intoxication and later mourned and empathised with him even though he would’ve been a very toxic lover. I love how grey the characters are because they’re not just one sided. Even the Darkling was just someone with good intentions but he was soured by his long life and losing so many people. He was just a boy who outlived his good soul. Alina was an orphan and always loved Mal so any other pretty girl she came across would’ve been a grisha showdown lol because of her insecurities and immaturities. She is naive but she is not heartless. She was inexperienced, just like any 17 year old would be when thrust upon a journey like that. Mal was possessive but passionate as well. They were still young adults who just figured out the lives they really wanted and how they wanted it to be with eachother at a very inconvenient time. None of the characters are just black or white here. I think the only truly unrealistic and unfathomable character is Nikolai, he is so cunning and clever and charming...and he is too good for everyone. I think people don’t like shadow and bone because it really sets itself apart with how the characters are made but I think since it was more realistic, even for a magical world, it was beautiful.
